title: Mamie Smith's disastrous Pittsburgh opening with Bubber Miley
summary: With Bubber Miley new to the stage, Mamie's costume trouble made the band repeat the introduction until her husband booted Bubber back on stage.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: This was still in New York City?

Originated in New York City, yes. I'll tell you, Johnny Dunn, the famous Johnny Dunn had quit so we hired Bubber Miley. I guess -- you know, he became very famous with Duke Ellington, and he had never been on stage before. And we opened in Pittsburgh, and Mamie had all new costumes made, and those days singers wore big feathers and plumes and there were no zippers -- it was all hook and eyes, you know.

And Mamie had this new costume, gorgeous costumes made so the opening day in Pittsburgh, at the Pershing Theater we played our first tune, 'Royal Garden Blues.' Bam -- played a 'vamp' big hand. All right. Now, we (unintelligible) right here for

you, if you don't get it, it ain't no fault of -- then the introduction bringing her on. No Mamie. So, her husband said, "Play the introduction again." We played it again, dah, dah, dah, dah. No Mamie. So he said, "Play the Royal Garden Blues again." Well, now, Bubber's scared to death. It's his first day on stage -- first time ever on stage, and his lip is giving out, so he played the Royal Garden Blues through and through, completely again, and the people applaud and say, "Hey, you played it once." So he said, "Play the introduction." Mamie's downstairs -- we don't know -- she's struggling with her costume. She's hooked up in the -- on the corner of her dresser and can't get it loose out of her dresser drawer -- and, I don't know -- everything happened. She couldn't get her dress on. Half on and half off. So, Bubber got excited and we played the introduction again and oh she said, "Play it again." By that time Bubber's frightened. I looked over there at Bubber and he was so nervous he had his trumpet down on his chin trying to blow it. And he's backing off of the stage at the same time. Backing up all at the same time and he's trying to find his mouth, scared to death. And her husband -- out to the wing, with Bubber backed off in the wing, and literally took his foot and booted him back on the stage, and the audience yelled. They had to bring the curtain down. Now, that was our first show in Pittsburgh.
Did it look like a great act?
Oh, it was a great act. The people screamed.
